question: How does the choice of cost function affect training behavior?
direct_answer: It changes the gradients, which changes how the model updates and what errors it prioritizes.
expanded_answer: Because optimization follows gradients of the cost, the chosen objective determines which mistakes are penalized more strongly and how learning proceeds. For example, some costs are more robust to outliers, while others strongly emphasize large errors.
common_wrong_ideas: The optimizer ignores the cost function shape
All costs produce the same updates
Only the model architecture controls training behavior
